Yes. Startup loads YAML, but Rust `Default` repeats its values; the existing
equality test detects drift rather than removing that second source. I will make
the committed YAML authoritative through one configuration owner that embeds,
deserializes and validates it once. `TacticalCombatConfig::default()` and the
existing subconfig defaults will project that value, preserving their callers
and values. The inspected deserializers have no `serde(default)` callbacks, and
validation does not read the runtime-config lock, so this route avoids recursive
defaults and lock acquisition. Invalid external YAML stays a fallible startup
error. Invalid compiled-in YAML is an internal invariant failure: `Default`
cannot return an error, so that case will have an explicit panic, with no
`unwrap`, `expect` or numeric fallback. The parser package is already locked;
this requires its tactical-core dependency edge rather than another package
version.
